walkthroughs.body_html:
Network Security — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Network Security brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Network Security.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: They are the same gate with different names.
OR is true when at least one input is true; XOR is true when exactly one input is true.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: Any item, randomly.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
The first one added (FIFO).
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Because TCP cannot handle video data.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
